part.text: {"variants":[{"id":"V1","title":"Full glycosylated capsid–receptor–glycan complexes instead of peptide fragments","text":"Model full 60-mer AAV capsids against membrane-anchored, glycosylated receptors — GPI-anchored ALPL, glycosylated LRP6 and CA-IV — with glycans included, using AlphaFold-Multimer for receptor domains, cryo-ET for the assembled complex and MD for pH-resolved contacts, rather than peptide–receptor-domain fragments in water. This would turn epitope geometry and pH-resolved contact kinetics into a computed prior for the actual glycosylated capsid–receptor–glycan complexes that Voyager's ALPL-NeuroShuttle and the Gradinaru lab's LRP6 mapping programme study. The root question still asks for which capsid–receptor binding signatures, but the signature now includes glycan and membrane context instead of only peptide-domain contacts. If the full-complex prior recovers receptor selectivity and pH-dependent release, it would give those programmes a structural rationale for receptor choice before Transwell or in vivo work.","root_link":"Bears on the \"for which capsid–receptor binding signatures\" half by asking whether epitope geometry and pH-resolved kinetics computed on the glycosylated, membrane-anchored complexes match the signatures the programmes actually select on.","compute_open":"Full 60-mer capsid–receptor–glycan systems are far larger than AlphaFold-Multimer runs of 5 models per capsid peptide and cryo-ET averaging of 85,135 symmetry-expanded particles, and it is unknown whether any affordable scale of computed coverage recovers glycan-dependent receptor selectivity; the only quantitative pH-resolved benchmark remains the single measured ALPL–VCAP-102 pair.","sequential":"The MD trajectory is still a chain of roughly 10^9–10^12 integration steps at about 2 fs each, each waiting on the previous coordinates, and full glycosylated 60-mer systems make each step more expensive; the answer can still be assembled from many independent replicas per (capsid, receptor, pH) condition, as in adaptive-sampling Markov state modelling that scaled linearly to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration.","changes":"Changes the system studied from peptide–receptor-domain fragments in water to full glycosylated capsid–receptor–glycan complexes, closing the gap that GPI-anchored ALPL, glycosylated LRP6, CA-IV and the 60-mer capsid context are absent; it also makes the result directly relevant to Voyager's ALPL-NeuroShuttle and the Gradinaru lab's LRP6 mapping."},{"id":"V2","title":"Cell-level Transwell transcytosis as the comparison","text":"Keep the AlphaFold-Multimer and pH-resolved MD calculations, but judge the computed signature against cell-level transcytosis — Transwell flux across human brain microvascular endothelial cells and receptor-knockout or knockdown blockade — for the same capsid–receptor pairs, rather than against its own 10-ns contact-survival labels or a 320-ns sequential run. The classifier would be calibrated to the endpoint Voyager's TRACER platform and the Gradinaru lab use when deciding whether a capsid crosses the BBB or stays in endothelium. A computed AUC would then mean separation of transcytosing from retained capsids in the assay those programmes trust, not separation of self-defined contact classes. If it fails, the negative result would also be interpretable against their decision endpoint rather than only against a proxy.","root_link":"Shifts the link from the computed signature alone to whether that signature predicts the cell-level transcytosis versus endothelial-retention outcome the programmes measure.","compute_open":"The structural and MD runs are unchanged, but the open quantity is now whether any computed signature correlates with Transwell flux and receptor blockade across multiple capsid–receptor pairs; no programme has published such a computed classifier, and the only measured pH-kinetics anchor is still ALPL–VCAP-102.","sequential":"Unchanged: one trajectory is a chain of roughly 10^9–10^12 ordered 2-fs steps, but the answer can be assembled from many short independent replicas per (capsid, receptor, pH) condition, with weak scaling of replicas as in adaptive-sampling Markov state modelling up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration.","changes":"Changes the comparison it is judged against from self-defined 10-ns contact labels and 320-ns runs to cell-level Transwell transcytosis plus receptor knockout, closing the gap that no programme has a computed classifier validated against cell-level transcytosis; aimed at Voyager's TRACER platform and the Gradinaru lab."},{"id":"V3","title":"Millisecond pH-resolved off-rates and release probabilities, not ten-ns contact survival","text":"Keep the peptide–receptor fragment system and AlphaFold-Multimer docking, but spend the extra compute on pH-resolved off-rates and endosomal-release probabilities estimated from many short replicas with adaptive-sampling Markov state models, rather than on ten-ns contact-survival proxies. Scale to roughly 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration, matching the adaptive-sampling precedent, and require error bars on the pH ratio for each capsid–receptor pair. The quantity bought is then a kinetic signature closer to the millisecond-scale off-rates and endosomal release steps that determine transcytosis, which is what Voyager, Dyno and the Gradinaru lab need to distinguish transport from retention. If the pH ratio does not separate at that scale, the negative result would rule out the kinetic-signature mechanism more strongly than the original ten-ns proxy could.","root_link":"Bears on the \"for which capsid–receptor binding signatures\" half by making pH-resolved kinetics a computed quantity with error bars rather than a ten-ns survival proxy.","compute_open":"The cited adaptive-sampling precedent reached linear wall-clock efficiency up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration, and the largest structural coverage cited is 5 AlphaFold-Multimer models per peptide with cryo-ET of 85,135 particles; what remains unknown is whether 5,000 short replicas per condition can estimate millisecond-scale pH-resolved off-rates accurately enough to classify transcytosis versus retention, since only ALPL–VCAP-102 has measured pH kinetics.","sequential":"One trajectory is still 10^9–10^12 ordered 2-fs steps, but the answer is assembled from many independent short trajectories; at 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration the weak scaling of independent replicas is the lever, as in adaptive-sampling Markov state modelling.","changes":"Changes the quantity more compute buys from ten-ns contact-survival proxies to pH-resolved off-rates and endosomal-release probabilities with error bars at 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration, closing the gap that ten-ns proxies are not the millisecond-scale off-rates or release steps that determine transcytosis."}]}
